questions.q: What is the first step this lesson recommends before naming or building any table for a new custom application?
options: Writing down the real entities — the actual "things" the app needs to track — before any screen or table exists
Opening Studio and clicking New Application Table immediately
Deciding which roles will have access, before anything else
Picking a table name that matches the application's scope prefix
questions.explain: Entity identification comes first: what real nouns does this application actually need to track, independent of any screen or table.

questions.q: In the Room Booking / Room example, what question decides whether an entity should extend `task`?
options: Whether it has a fixed number of fields
Whether it needs to be routed, approved, or tracked through a state machine
Whether it will be used by more than one department
Whether it was created before or after the application's scope
questions.explain: The deciding question is whether the entity needs lifecycle, routing, or approval behavior — exactly what `task` already provides.

questions.q: Why is a standalone table (no parent) the right design for the Room table, rather than extending `task`?
options: Standalone tables load faster than tables that extend task
A Room has no lifecycle, assignment, or approval behavior — inheriting a state field and an assignment_group field would only confuse a static reference record
Room records can never have a reference field pointing at them
Extending task is only allowed for tables created in the global scope
questions.explain: Room is static, descriptive data with no workflow — giving it task's state and assignment fields would add confusing, unused behavior.

questions.q: What does the planned `room` reference field on Room Booking actually store, versus what it displays?
options: It stores a free-text room name and displays the same text
It stores and displays the exact same value, with no distinction
It stores a sys_id pointing at the Room record while displaying a readable value, such as the room's name
It stores a list of every room ever booked by that employee
questions.explain: A reference field stores a sys_id underneath while displaying a readable value — the same pattern Course 2 covered for any reference field.

questions.q: What is the "reverse view" of the Room Booking → Room reference field, planned in this lesson but built in Lesson 25?
options: A related list on the Room form showing every booking that points back at that room
A second reference field added to the Room table pointing back at Room Booking
A duplicate copy of the Room table inside the Room Booking table
A UI Policy that hides the room field on weekends
questions.explain: A related list on the Room record's form is the reverse view of the reference field — the same related-list pattern from Course 2.
